Which integral is obtained?

$$
\int \frac{3}{\sqrt{1 - 16 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "cc411b53-59e8-5c6e-aca6-364024091383" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=4 x$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(4)\,\mathrm{d}x$.

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{1}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $3\cdot \frac{1}{4}=\frac{3}{4}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{\sqrt{1 - 16 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{3}{4}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

The transformed integral is

$$
\frac{3}{4}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).
$$"] [:db/add "cc411b53-59e8-5c6e-aca6-364024091383" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "cc411b53-59e8-5c6e-aca6-364024091383" :question/answer-fields "2e80ba22-bb42-55e2-8a66-bf30eeae5992"] [:db/ensure "cc411b53-59e8-5c6e-aca6-364024091383" :question/validate] [:db/add 17592186064218 :knowledge-point/questions "cc411b53-59e8-5c6e-aca6-364024091383"] [:db/add "f6366d5e-ecb7-5c60-8d27-7983a72a9d19" :answer/id #uuid "f6366d5e-ecb7-5c60-8d27-7983a72a9d19"] [:db/add "f6366d5e-ecb7-5c60-8d27-7983a72a9d19" :answer/type :answer.type/math] [:db/add "f6366d5e-ecb7-5c60-8d27-7983a72a9d19" :answer/value "2\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - "96100969-066d-5014-b021-b96b25f2b3b9" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{2}{\sqrt{9 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

You may use $\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C$.

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "96100969-066d-5014-b021-b96b25f2b3b9" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{3}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{3})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{9 - x^{2}}=3\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{3})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=3\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{2}{3}\cdot 3=2$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{2}{\sqrt{9 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=2\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the supplied primitive:

$$
2\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=2\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
2\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{x}{3} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "96100969-066d-5014-b021-b96b25f2b3b9" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "96100969-066d-5014-b021-b96b25f2b3b9" :question/answer-fields $$

$$

"3bcbd307-7eb0-5749-9f39-f59ad0eeb13c"] [:db/add "3bcbd307-7eb0-5749-9f39-f59ad0eeb13c" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{4}{\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

You may use $\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C$.

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "3bcbd307-7eb0-5749-9f39-f59ad0eeb13c" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{4}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{4})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}=4\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{4})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=4\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $1\cdot 4=4$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=4\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the supplied primitive:

$$
4\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=4\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

"94bdb05f-43fe-5e78-b307-235e180d305b" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{3}{\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

You may use $\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C$.

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "94bdb05f-43fe-5e78-b307-235e180d305b" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{4}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{4})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}=4\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{4})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=4\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{3}{4}\cdot 4=3$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=3\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the supplied primitive:

$$
3\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=3\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
3\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{x}{4} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "94bdb05f-43fe-5e78-b307-235e180d305b" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "94bdb05f-43fe-5e78-b307-235e180d305b" :question/answer-fields $$
2\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=2\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
2\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{2 x}{5} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "2a55d7ae-9d4b-5c96-84f9-d74247a5e8d5" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "2a55d7ae-9d4b-5c96-84f9-d74247a5e8d5" :question/answer-fields "94849f5f-2cf8-5cf1-8a7d-c7ccc0fffc35" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{4}{\sqrt{9 - 16 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{9 - 16 x^{2}}=3\sqrt{1-(\frac{4 x}{3})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{3}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{4}{3}\cdot \frac{3}{4}=1$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{\sqrt{9 - 16 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the supplied primitive:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\arcsin{\left(\frac{4 x}{3} \right)}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "94849f5f-2cf8-5cf1-8a7d-c7ccc0fffc35" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "94849f5f-2cf8-5cf1-8a7d-c7ccc0fffc35" :question/answer-fields "df9de8b9-2f01-568f-aeb5-4514cd0a2608" :question/id #uuid "df9de8b9-2f01-568f-aeb5-4514cd0a2608"] [:db/add "df9de8b9-2f01-568f-aeb5-4514cd0a2608" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 - 9 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

You may use $\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C$.

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "df9de8b9-2f01-568f-aeb5-4514cd0a2608" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{3 x}{2}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{3}{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{4 - 9 x^{2}}=2\sqrt{1-(\frac{3 x}{2})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{2}{3}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{2}{3}=\frac{1}{3}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 - 9 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the supplied primitive:

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{3}\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{3 x}{2} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "df9de8b9-2f01-568f-aeb5-4514cd0a2608" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "df9de8b9-2f01-568f-aeb5-4514cd0a2608" :question/answer-fields "96100969-066d-5014-b021-b96b25f2b3b9" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{2}{\sqrt{9 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

You may use $\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C$.

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "96100969-066d-5014-b021-b96b25f2b3b9" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{3}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{3})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{9 - x^{2}}=3\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{3})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=3\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{2}{3}\cdot 3=2$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{2}{\sqrt{9 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=2\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the supplied primitive:

$$
2\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=2\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
2\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{x}{3} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "96100969-066d-5014-b021-b96b25f2b3b9" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "96100969-066d-5014-b021-b96b25f2b3b9" :question/answer-fields $$

$$

"3bcbd307-7eb0-5749-9f39-f59ad0eeb13c"] [:db/add "3bcbd307-7eb0-5749-9f39-f59ad0eeb13c" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{4}{\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

You may use $\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C$.

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "3bcbd307-7eb0-5749-9f39-f59ad0eeb13c" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{4}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{4})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}=4\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{4})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=4\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $1\cdot 4=4$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=4\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the supplied primitive:

$$
4\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=4\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

"94bdb05f-43fe-5e78-b307-235e180d305b" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{3}{\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

You may use $\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C$.

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "94bdb05f-43fe-5e78-b307-235e180d305b" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{4}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{4})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}=4\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{4})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=4\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{3}{4}\cdot 4=3$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=3\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the supplied primitive:

$$
3\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=3\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
3\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{x}{4} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "94bdb05f-43fe-5e78-b307-235e180d305b" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "94bdb05f-43fe-5e78-b307-235e180d305b" :question/answer-fields $$
2\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=2\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
2\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{2 x}{5} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "2a55d7ae-9d4b-5c96-84f9-d74247a5e8d5" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "2a55d7ae-9d4b-5c96-84f9-d74247a5e8d5" :question/answer-fields "94849f5f-2cf8-5cf1-8a7d-c7ccc0fffc35" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{4}{\sqrt{9 - 16 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{9 - 16 x^{2}}=3\sqrt{1-(\frac{4 x}{3})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{3}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{4}{3}\cdot \frac{3}{4}=1$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{\sqrt{9 - 16 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the supplied primitive:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\arcsin{\left(\frac{4 x}{3} \right)}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "94849f5f-2cf8-5cf1-8a7d-c7ccc0fffc35" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "94849f5f-2cf8-5cf1-8a7d-c7ccc0fffc35" :question/answer-fields "df9de8b9-2f01-568f-aeb5-4514cd0a2608" :question/id #uuid "df9de8b9-2f01-568f-aeb5-4514cd0a2608"] [:db/add "df9de8b9-2f01-568f-aeb5-4514cd0a2608" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 - 9 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

You may use $\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C$.

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "df9de8b9-2f01-568f-aeb5-4514cd0a2608" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{3 x}{2}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{3}{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{4 - 9 x^{2}}=2\sqrt{1-(\frac{3 x}{2})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{2}{3}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{2}{3}=\frac{1}{3}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 - 9 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the supplied primitive:

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{3}\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{3 x}{2} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "df9de8b9-2f01-568f-aeb5-4514cd0a2608" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "df9de8b9-2f01-568f-aeb5-4514cd0a2608" :question/answer-fields \int \frac{4}{\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] ["3bcbd307-7eb0-5749-9f39-f59ad0eeb13c" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{4}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{4})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}=4\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{4})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=4\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $1\cdot 4=4$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=4\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the supplied primitive:

$$
4\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=4\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
4\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{x}{4} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] ["3bcbd307-7eb0-5749-9f39-f59ad0eeb13c" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["3bcbd307-7eb0-5749-9f39-f59ad0eeb13c" :question/answer-fields "f744ca99-c16f-5a9f-b4b6-91fd8f5bbd78"] ["94849f5f-2cf8-5cf1-8a7d-c7ccc0fffc35" :question/id #uuid "94849f5f-2cf8-5cf1-8a7d-c7ccc0fffc35"] ["94849f5f-2cf8-5cf1-8a7d-c7ccc0fffc35" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{4}{\sqrt{9 - 16 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{9 - 16 x^{2}}=3\sqrt{1-(\frac{4 x}{3})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{3}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{4}{3}\cdot \frac{3}{4}=1$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{\sqrt{9 - 16 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the supplied primitive:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\arcsin{\left(\frac{4 x}{3} \right)}+C.
$$"] ["94849f5f-2cf8-5cf1-8a7d-c7ccc0fffc35" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] ["94849f5f-2cf8-5cf1-8a7d-c7ccc0fffc35" :question/answer-fields "a05b84b7-cde5-5dcd-8b23-dd8470aad214"] Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{4 - 9 x^{2}}=2\sqrt{1-(\frac{3 x}{2})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{2}{3}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{2}{3}=\frac{1}{3}$.

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 - 9 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the supplied primitive:

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{3}\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$

["ac7ccb86-e562-5c18-93ff-df4783c50a60" :question/id #uuid "ac7ccb86-e562-5c18-93ff-df4783c50a60"] ["ac7ccb86-e562-5c18-93ff-df4783c50a60" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 - 16 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

You may use $\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C$.

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] ["ac7ccb86-e562-5c18-93ff-df4783c50a60" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=2 x$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(2)\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{4 - 16 x^{2}}=2\sqrt{1-(2 x)^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{4}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 - 16 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{4}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the supplied primitive:

$$
\frac{1}{4}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{4}\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{1}{4}\left(\arcsin{\left(2 x \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] ["ac7ccb86-e562-5c18-93ff-df4783c50a60" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] ["ac7ccb86-e562-5c18-93ff-df4783c50a60" :question/answer-fields "78a2c40b-4f5e-5b3d-a066-8a1ca5b2c47a"] $$

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{9 - 4 x^{2}}=3\sqrt{1-(\frac{2 x}{3})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{3}{2}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $1\cdot \frac{3}{2}=\frac{3}{2}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{\sqrt{9 - 4 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{3}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the supplied primitive:

$$
\frac{3}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{3}{2}\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{3}{2}\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{2 x}{3} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] ["7ae327cb-d047-56a3-9c96-709a008c4721" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] ["7ae327cb-d047-56a3-9c96-709a008c4721" :question/answer-fields "1df600e8-2b95-509c-9eca-984825d6041e"]
